idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after v2.3.1 was deployed to production (unhealthy, error rate 18%; v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging). Rolled back in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped partway with an orchestrator error after us-east, leaving regions on mixed versions. A second attempt finished the rollout. Current state: v2.3.0 in all regions, healthy, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and look into why v2.3.1 was promoted when its RC was unhealthy in staging. Also investigate the orchestrator error.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions and healthy again, and SEV2 incident **INC-0001** is open.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. The bad release, v2.3.1, also failed as a test build in staging. The first rollback attempt stopped with an orchestrator error after us-east, leaving the other two regions on v2.3.1. I ran the same rollback again and it finished. us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0 now, and the error rate dropped from 18% to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback, the region outage partway through and the current state. It also suggests follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, look into why v2.3.1 went to production after failing in staging, and investigate the orchestrator error. The first attempt to open the incident timed out, so I retried with the same request key. That key stops the system creating a duplicate, so you should only see one incident and one page.

content.text: The rollback only finished in us-east. Rolling back to a known-healthy version is safe to repeat, so I'll try once more to finish the other regions.
